# Stage 2: Experimenting with New Processing

We will test a range of transformations on the data before clustering to see if it is able to create a more informative representation of deformation. The approaches are:

1.  Moving average
2.  Piecewise linear regression / linear spline regression
3.  Feature selection
4.  PCA ? - only if time

We will also look at filtering the data based on coherence, as done in Rana et al.'s paper. Adding to our stage 1 clustering baseline, we will apply the same clustering, but on the standardised data. Although, our initial hypothesis with using the standardised data is that it may not be as informative as using the raw displacement values. This is due to all acquisitions being in the same scale, and therefore standardising the data may remove the meaningfulness of measurement difference.

```{r}
# Helper function for removing baseline date column

remove_zero_var <- function(x) {

  x[, col_sd > 0, drop = FALSE]
```

## 2. Moving Averages

We will test three values of window size using moving average:

- 2: 2 acquisitions are averaged out, meaning one window summarises 12 \* 2 = 24 days.

- 3: 3 acquisitions are averaged out, meaning one window summarises 12 \* 3 = 36 days.

- 5: 5 acquisitions are averaged out, meaning one window summarises 12 \* 5 = 60 days.

```{r}
# Cadia

# MA(2)
cadia_MA2 <- t(apply(cadia_D, 1, function(x) {
  rollmean(x, k = 2, align = "right", fill = NA)
}))

#cadia_MA2 <- cadia_MA2[, -1]

# MA(3)
cadia_MA3 <- t(apply(cadia_D, 1, function(x) {
  rollmean(x, k = 3, align = "right", fill = NA)
}))

#cadia_MA3 <- cadia_MA3[, -c(1:2)]
```

#### Silhouette Score

```{r}
# Average Silhouette Score Helper Function
avg_sil_score <- function(hc, d_mat, k_vals = 2:5){
  
  avg_sil <- numeric(length(k_vals))
  
  for(i in seq_along(k_vals)){
    
    clusters <- cutree(hc, k = k_vals[i])
    sil_score <- silhouette(clusters, d_mat)
    avg_sil[i] <- mean(sil_score[, 3])
    
  }
  
  data.frame(
    k = k_vals,
    avg_silhouette_score = avg_sil
  )
}
```

We'll compute the silhouette score for k = 2, 3, 4 and 5.

```{r}
# Cadia
cadia_hc_sil <- avg_sil_score(cadia_hc, cadia_dist)

# MA(2)
cadia_MA2_hc_sil <- avg_sil_score(
  cadia_MA2_hc,
  cadia_MA2_dist
)

# MA(3)
cadia_MA3_hc_sil <- avg_sil_score(
  cadia_MA3_hc,
  cadia_MA3_dist
)
```

The moving average dataset of the hierarchical clustering using a window size of 3 achieved the highest average silhouette score for k = 2. Both moving average datasets result in the highest silhouette score at k = 2 and as k increases, the silhouette score decreases.

#### Silhouette Score

```{r}
# Helper function for K-means
avg_sil_score_km <- function(km_models, d_mat){
  
  avg_sil <- numeric(length(km_models))
  
  for(i in seq_along(km_models)){
    
    sil_score <- silhouette(
      km_models[[i]]$cluster,
      d_mat
    )
    
    avg_sil[i] <- mean(sil_score[,3])
    
  }
  
  data.frame(
    k = 2:5,
    avg_silhouette_score = avg_sil
  )
  
}
```

#### Davies-Bouldin Index

```{r}
# Davies-Bouldin Index Helper function
dbi_km <- function(data, km_models, k_vals = 2:5) {
  
  db_vals <- numeric(length(km_models))
  
  for (i in seq_along(k_vals)) {
    db_vals[i] <- index.DB(
      data,
      km_models[[i]]$cluster
    )$DB
  }
  
  data.frame(
    k = k_vals,
    davies_bouldin = db_vals
  )
}
```

## 3. Piecewise Linear Regression

As clustering can be strongly influenced by displacement magnitude and fluctuations, we continue to test methods that smooth out and work with outliers.

The spline approach represents each time series by its rate of deformation over successive time intervals. It may be able to identify and distinguish different deformation behaviours based on changes in velocity/slope.

We'll use the data represented in matrices that still include the baseline date with 0 to use for the first slope.

```{r}
dim(cadia_D_mat)
```

```{r}
# Extracting actual date names
  # note that all dates are from a descending orbit track

cadia_dates <- as.Date(sub("D_", "", colnames(cadia_D_mat)), format = "%Y%m%d")

cadia_dates
```

Piecewise linear models partition the data into segments and fit separate linear regression models to each segment. It allows for broad average trends in the data to be captured while maintaining simplicity and interpretability.

Each segment is divided to make almost linear sections. An index feature is used to model the marginal change of one unit of time. When a series has break points in the trend, we add a knot to each break point:

- A knot feature allows us to inform the model of a change in the trend slope.

- Left to the knot point equals 0, right to the knot is an arbitrage numbers that increase as a function of time.

Instead of treating the columns as observations 1, 2, 3..., we will use elapsed days: 0, 12, 24, 36, 60, etc.

```{r}
cadia_time <- as.numeric(cadia_dates - cadia_dates[1])

cadia_time
```

```{r}
diff(cadia_dates)
```

We choose fixed knots, initially testing 60-day intervals (and the satellite capturing measurements in 12-day intervals).

Define our knots:

```{r}
cadia_knots <- seq(60, max(cadia_time) - 60, by = 60)

cadia_knots
```

```{r}
# Apply spline regression

y <- cadia_D_mat[1, ]

X <- data.frame(time = cadia_time)

for(k in cadia_knots) {
  X[[paste0("knot_", k)]] <- pmax(0, cadia_time - k)
}

cadia_model_data <- cbind(data.frame(displacement = y), X)

cadia_test_fit <- lm(displacement ~ ., data = cadia_model_data)
```

```{r}
png(
  "cadia_piecewise_dendrogram.png",
  width = 2400,
  height = 1800,
  res = 300
)

plot(
  cadia_dates,
  y,
  type = "o",
  xlab = "Date",
  ylab = "Cumulative displacement (mm)",
  main = "Cadia: Piecewise Linear Fit"
)

lines(
  cadia_dates,
  fitted(cadia_test_fit),
  lwd = 2
)

abline(
  v = cadia_dates[1] + cadia_knots,
  lty = 2
)

dev.off()
```

Extracting the slopes from the fitted model for clustering:

```{r}
cadia_coefs <- coef(cadia_test_fit)

cadia_coefs
```

```{r}
# Remove intercept
cadia_slope_changes <- cadia_coefs[-1]

# convert slope changes into actual slope for each interval
cadia_test_slopes <- cumsum(cadia_slope_changes)

cadia_test_slopes
```

```{r}
# ^^^^ Process as a function

extract_piecewise_slopes <- function(displacement, time, knots) {
  
  # Design matrix
  X <- data.frame(time = time)
  
  for(k in knots) {
    X[[paste0("knot_", k)]] <- pmax(0, time - k)
  }
  
  # Add displacement
  model_data <- cbind(
    data.frame(displacement = displacement),
    X
  )
  
  # Fit continuous piecewise-linear regression
  fit <- lm(
    displacement ~ .,
    data = model_data
  )
  
  # Remove intercept
  slope_changes <- coef(fit)[-1]
  
  # Actual slope in each interval
  interval_slopes <- cumsum(slope_changes)
  
  names(interval_slopes) <- paste0(
    "Slope_", seq_along(interval_slopes)
  )
  
  return(interval_slopes)
}
```

```{r}
test_slopes <- extract_piecewise_slopes(
  displacement = cadia_D_mat[1, ],
  time = cadia_time,
  knots = cadia_knots
)

test_slopes
```

```{r}
cadia_test_slopes
```

```{r}
# apply to every cadia ob

cadia_piecewise <- t(apply(cadia_D_mat, 1, extract_piecewise_slopes, time = cadia_time, knots = cadia_knots))
```

```{r}
dim(cadia_piecewise)

head(cadia_piecewise)

anyNA(cadia_piecewise)
```

We've converted the original data from 12502 x 45 displacement values to 12502 x \~9 slope values.

## 5. Standardised Data

We standardise each row's displacement values:

```{r}
# Cadia
cadia_std <- t(
  scale(
    t(cadia_D)
  )
)

dim(cadia_std)
anyNA(cadia_std)
```

- NA = TRUE. We identify this row(s) and decide whether to change the row values or delete it entirely.

```{r}
# Standard deviation of each time series
cadia_row_sd <- apply(cadia_D, 1, sd)

# Rows that can actually be standardised
cadia_valid_rows <- cadia_row_sd != 0

sum(!cadia_valid_rows)
```

- As it is only one row, we delete it.

```{r}
cadia_std <- t(
  scale(
    t(cadia_D[cadia_valid_rows, ])
  )
)

dim(cadia_std)
anyNA(cadia_std)
```

```{r}
cadia_std_km_5 <- kmeans(
  cadia_std,
  centers = 5,
  nstart = 20
)
```

#### Silhouette Score

```{r}
cadia_std_km_sil <- avg_sil_score_km(
  list(cadia_std_km_2,
       cadia_std_km_3,
       cadia_std_km_4,
       cadia_std_km_5),
  cadia_std_dist
)

cadia_std_km_sil
```

#### Davies-Bouldin Index

```{r}
cadia_std_km_db <- dbi_km(
  cadia_std,
  list(cadia_std_km_2,
       cadia_std_km_3,
       cadia_std_km_4,
       cadia_std_km_5)
)

cadia_std_km_db
```

```{r}
p_db_cadia_std <- ggplot(
  cadia_std_km_db,
  aes(
    x = k,
    y = davies_bouldin
  )
) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2:5) +
  labs(
    title = "Davies–Bouldin Index: Cadia (Standardised)",
    x = "Number of clusters",
    y = "Davies–Bouldin index"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
ggsave(
  "cadia_dbi_std.png",
  p_db_cadia_std,
  width = 7,
  height = 5,
  dpi = 300
)
```

#### Apply cluster IDs and export

We have to keep in mind that after standardising, one of the rows was deleted as it led to only zero values. So applying the cluster IDs is a different process here.

```{r}
# Create empty cols
cadia$std_km_2 <- NA_integer_
cadia$std_km_3 <- NA_integer_
cadia$std_km_4 <- NA_integer_
cadia$std_km_5 <- NA_integer_

# Fill only rows that were included in standardisation
cadia$std_km_2[cadia_valid_rows] <- cadia_std_km_2$cluster
cadia$std_km_3[cadia_valid_rows] <- cadia_std_km_3$cluster
cadia$std_km_4[cadia_valid_rows] <- cadia_std_km_4$cluster
cadia$std_km_5[cadia_valid_rows] <- cadia_std_km_5$cluster
```

```{r}
cadia[7424, c(
  "std_km_2",
  "std_km_3",
  "std_km_4",
  "std_km_5"
)]
```

```{r}
table(cadia$std_km_2, useNA = "ifany")
```

```{r}
write.csv(
  cadia,
  "cadia_std_km.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```
